options.B: For every payment on every electronic payment system in which the bank participates, the bank stores the amount, timing, processing steps, routing, payer, payee, system used and any suspensions, so it can derive its net settlement-account position at the close of business only.

question: A regulator at a U.K. supervisor (GBP reporting) notes that, in a trade repository, most of the aggregate credit default swap (CDS) notional is in dealer-to-dealer positions rather than dealer-to-client positions. options.A: Compression trades, applied to redundant or nearly redundant positions among dealers, have increased the dealer-to-dealer notional by adding new offsetting contracts to each dealer’s book.
options.B: When a hedge fund reduces a CDS position, the original dealer typically assigns the position to a central clearing counterparty, which then stands between the fund and the dealer.
options.C: When a hedge fund reduces a CDS position, the fund itself typically steps in between two dealers by entering new back-to-back CDS positions with each of them.

**Concept and theory**

Dealers are especially likely to be counterparties to other dealers in credit default swaps (CDS), which are in essence insurance against the default of a named borrower. The mechanism is novation. When a hedge fund wants to reduce a CDS position, a typical step is to have its original position novated to another dealer. question: An internal auditor at a French bank is writing up case studies on dealer banks. question:
A member of the board risk committee at a Canadian bank holding company is reviewing a briefing on how a large dealer bank can fail when its solvency is questioned. The briefing contains the following statements:

I. As with a depositor run at a commercial bank, fears over the dealer’s solvency lead those dealing with it to act so as to reduce their potential losses in the event of its default.

II. The first and most decisive mechanism in the collapse is the flight of short-term secured creditors; the later loss of clearing-bank privileges is a secondary consequence.

III. Unlike insured depositors, many parties exposed to a dealer bank have no default insurance, or do not wish to bear the frictional costs of involvement in its failure procedures even if they are insured.

IV. Because derivatives counterparties hold collateral against the dealer, their actions to lower their exposures leave the dealer’s cash position unchanged.

options.D: III only

solution:
Board briefing: which statements on dealer-bank run mechanics are correct.

Duffie frames dealer-bank failure as a new form of bank run. The economic core is the same as a classic depositor run: when the bank’s solvency is questioned, everyone with an exposure acts to reduce the loss they would suffer if it defaulted, and the collective rush can turn a solvency scare into a cash insolvency (a self-fulfilling prophecy). What differs are the institutional mechanisms and the systemic destructiveness. Insured depositors have little reason to race each other, but most parties exposed to a dealer bank have no default insurance, or would rather not bear the frictional costs of being caught up in the failure procedures even if insured, so they leave early.

Which of the following best describes the reasoning that, according to the reading, makes non-renewal likely?

options.B: The haircut fully insulates the fund from any decline in the collateral’s value, so non-renewal reflects only a regulatory cap on the fund’s exposure to any single dealer bank.
